title: Dashboards, components, dynamic dashboards, subscriptions, and folders
objectives: Explain a dashboard as a page of widgets (Classic: components) sourced from reports, not as a second copy of the data.
Choose a specified running user versus a dynamic dashboard that shows each viewer their own data.
Apply folder Viewer/Editor/Manager sharing and know Editor does not by itself grant report-edit rights.
Cite Help limits: dynamic dashboard counts by edition, no schedule or subscribe on dynamic dashboards, widget and subscription caps.
diagnostic_question: A VP wants every sales rep to open the same dashboard and see only their pipeline, emailed weekly. Do you use one dynamic dashboard with a subscription, clone folders per rep, or refuse part of the request—and why?
definition: A dashboard is a page of widgets (called components in Classic) that visualize source reports. A dynamic dashboard shows each user the data they can access, instead of a single specified running user. Folders control who can find and save dashboards; subscriptions email a snapshot on a schedule. You cannot subscribe to or schedule refreshes for a dynamic dashboard. ([Dynamic Dashboards](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.dashboards_dynamic_overview.htm); [Limits](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.rd_reports_dashboards_limits.htm))
why_it_matters: The interview trap is 'dynamic plus subscribe.' Help forbids subscribing to dynamic dashboards and scheduling their refreshes. Folder Editor access is not the same as Run Reports or Modify All Data. Widgets have their own grouping caps. Dashboards are metadata; the numbers they show are report queries against business data.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a hotel lobby video wall. Each screen (widget) is fed by a camera (source report). A specified running user is one security guard's badge on every camera. A dynamic dashboard is each guest's keycard: they only see their floor. Folders are the concierge keys to the control room. Subscriptions are the morning newspaper slipped under the door—but Help will not deliver that newspaper for a keycard-personalized wall; dynamic dashboards must be refreshed manually and cannot be subscribed.
deeper_explanation: Dynamic dashboards provide individualized views without separate dashboards and folders. They show each user only the data they can access. Available in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer Editions. Creating them requires Manage Dynamic Dashboards. Managers with View My Team's Dashboards or View All Data can preview as users beneath them. ([Dynamic Dashboards](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.dashboards_dynamic_overview.htm))

Edition caps: up to 5 dynamic dashboards in Enterprise, 10 in Unlimited and Performance, 3 in Developer. You cannot save a dynamic dashboard in a private folder, cannot schedule refreshes, cannot subscribe, and deleted dashboards in the recycle bin still count until permanently deleted. ([Dynamic Dashboards](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.dashboards_dynamic_overview.htm))

Each dashboard can have up to 25 widgets, including a maximum of 20 charts and tables, 3 images, and 25 rich text widgets. A widget can calculate up to 1,000 groupings. Dashboard filters: 5 per dashboard, up to 50 values. You cannot subscribe to a dynamic dashboard; dashboard filters are not applied to emailed dashboards. ([Limits](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.rd_reports_dashboards_limits.htm))

Folder Editor access lets you view and save items in the folder but does not by itself determine access to contents: you still need permissions such as Run Reports to run, and you cannot give Editor access to standard report folders. ([Editor Access to Report and Dashboard Folders](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.analytics_folder_editor.htm))

Subscriptions: Unlimited Edition users can subscribe to up to 15 reports and 15 dashboards; other orgs 7 and 7. Each subscription supports up to 500 recipients. The folder must be shared with recipients. Org can schedule up to 500 dashboard and 500 report subscriptions on a given hour of a given day. ([Limits](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=analytics.rd_reports_dashboards_limits.htm))

mental_model.analogy: A hotel lobby video wall: widgets are screens, source reports are cameras, specified running user is one guard's badge, dynamic is each guest's keycard, folders are concierge keys, subscriptions are newspapers that Help will not send for keycard walls.
useful_mapping: specified running user → one badge for every viewer
dynamic dashboard → each guest sees their own floor
manual refresh on dynamic → you walk to the wall; it does not auto-print
where_it_breaks: Hotels do not cap you at 5 or 10 personalized walls by 'edition.'
Emailed dashboards drop dashboard filters—newspapers would not silently drop the weather box.
Editor folder access still needs Run Reports to run a report inside.
Recycle-bin dynamic dashboards still counting is unlike a hotel taking a TV off the wall.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Dashboards are walls of widgets fed by reports. Specified running user is one person's access for everyone. Dynamic is each viewer's access—but you cannot subscribe or schedule refresh, and editions cap how many you may have. Folders are not the same as Run Reports.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I never pair 'dynamic' with 'email me every Monday' as one design. Help forbids subscribe and scheduled refresh on dynamic dashboards; they must be refreshed manually and cannot live in a private folder. If leadership needs a shared emailed snapshot, I use a specified running user whose access matches the intended audience, share the folder, and subscribe within 500 recipients and per-user 7 or 15 caps. If each rep must see only their rows live, I use dynamic within the 5/10/3 edition cap and tell them to open it in the app. Editor on a folder does not let you edit a report without the right permission.

terminology.plain: A page of charts and tables sourced from reports.
terminology.precise: Metadata that references reports as widgets. Classic calls widgets components.
terminology.example: A LAB Sales wall with a pipeline chart and a table of stuck deals.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: CRM Analytics dashboard (ANA-006): a different product.
terminology.boundary: Dashboards do not store a second copy of Opportunity rows.

terminology.plain: One chart, table, metric, image, or rich-text panel on a dashboard.
terminology.precise: Up to 25 widgets; max 20 charts/tables; max 3 images. Calculates up to 1,000 groupings.
terminology.example: A gauge sourced from a summary Opportunities report.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Report chart on the report page itself.
terminology.boundary: Custom LWCs on dashboards are not shown in subscription emails.

terminology.plain: Whose record access the dashboard uses when it queries.
terminology.precise: Specified user: everyone sees that user's data. Dynamic: each viewer sees their own.
terminology.example: Specified as the Sales Ops analyst so the whole company sees the same snapshot.
terminology.non_example: The person who last edited the dashboard folder.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Dashboard owner: ownership transfer is a different feature.
terminology.boundary: View Dashboard As / team preview requires View My Team's Dashboards or View All Data.

terminology.plain: A dashboard that personalizes to each viewer's access.
terminology.precise: EE 5, UE/PE 10, DE 3. No private folder, no scheduled refresh, no subscribe. Recycle bin counts.
terminology.example: One pipeline wall every rep opens, seeing only their Opportunities.
terminology.non_example: A specified-user dashboard emailed on Mondays.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Dashboard filter for a product: a filter is not a running-user mode.
terminology.boundary: Manage Dynamic Dashboards permission is required to create them.

terminology.plain: Email a dashboard snapshot on a schedule.
terminology.precise: Not available for dynamic dashboards. Filters not applied in the email. Folder must be shared. 500 recipients; UE 15/15 else 7/7 per user.
terminology.example: Monday 8am email of the specified-user forecast dashboard to a role.
terminology.non_example: A report chart on a Lightning home page.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Scheduled dashboard refresh (different allocation in the limits table).
terminology.boundary: Unique count or field-to-field filters on the source report can block refresh of a subscription.

terminology.plain: Who can find reports and dashboards in a folder.
terminology.precise: Enhanced folder sharing: Viewer, Editor, Manager. Editor is not a substitute for Run Reports.
terminology.example: Share LAB_Sales_Dashboards with the West role as Viewer.
terminology.non_example: OWD on Opportunity (that is record sharing, ANA-005).
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Library in Files (APP track), not this folder.
terminology.boundary: Standard report folders cannot be given Editor access.

terminology.plain: A picker on the dashboard that subsets widgets that support it.
terminology.precise: 5 filters per dashboard; a filter can have up to 50 values. Not applied to emailed dashboards.
terminology.example: Product family filter on a specified-user product dashboard.
terminology.non_example: A report field filter saved on the source report (ANA-003).
terminology.boundary: Do not promise emailed subscribers will see the filter you clicked before sending.

terminology.plain: One named user whose access the dashboard always uses.
terminology.precise: Everyone who can open the dashboard sees that user's data, not their own, unless you use dynamic instead.
terminology.example: Run as the VP of Sales so regional managers see the same rolled-up numbers.
terminology.non_example: Each manager seeing only their team without View My Team's Dashboards on a specified peer.
terminology.boundary: If the specified user loses access to Opportunities, the wall goes blank for everyone.

when_to_use: When stakeholders need a page of charts and tables sourced from existing reports rather than a single report.
When every viewer must see their own rows: a dynamic dashboard, if the edition cap allows and they will refresh live.
When the company needs one shared snapshot: a specified running user plus folder sharing, optionally a subscription.
When you must explain folder Editor versus Run Reports, and why standard report folders cannot be Editor-shared.
when_not_to_use: Do not subscribe to a dynamic dashboard or schedule its refresh; Help forbids both.
Do not use a dashboard as a substitute for fixing the report type, format, or filters (ANA-001–003).
Do not assume folder Editor lets someone change report metadata without the matching user permission.
Do not expect emailed dashboards to honor the dashboard filters you selected on screen.

interview_questions.question: What is a dashboard, and how do widgets relate to reports?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A dashboard is a page of widgets—charts, tables, metrics—each sourced from a report. It is metadata. It does not store a second Opportunity database. Classic calls widgets components.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I build reports first (type, format, filters). Then I assemble a wall of up to 25 widgets, with at most 20 charts or tables. Each widget queries through its source report and the dashboard's running user. Folder sharing decides who finds the wall; Run Reports still matters. I keep CRM Analytics dashboards out of this answer; that is a later product.
interview_questions.example: LAB pipeline chart plus a stuck-deals table, both pointing at summary reports in a shared folder.
weak_answer_warnings: Saying the dashboard copies all rows

interview_questions.question: Specified running user versus dynamic dashboard?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Specified: one user's access for every viewer—good for a shared snapshot. Dynamic: each viewer sees their own data—good for a personal wall. Dynamic cannot subscribe or schedule refresh.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I pick based on the audience. Company forecast emailed Monday is specified as Sales Ops. Reps opening the same definition for 'my pipeline' is dynamic, within 5/10/3, not in a private folder, recycled copies still counting. Managers with View My Team's Dashboards can preview subordinates. I never claim dynamic emails. I treat a specified user with View All Data as a security review.
interview_questions.example: Two LAB dashboards: specified for the email, dynamic for live personalization.

interview_questions.question: Design 'one wall, every rep, only their data, Monday email.'
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I refuse the single-feature version. Live personalization is dynamic. Monday email is a specified-user dashboard (or report subscriptions) because Help forbids dynamic subscribe.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I split the requirement. Dynamic dashboard in a shared folder, manual refresh, edition cap checked, recycle bin empty. Separate specified-user dashboard subscribed to a role under 500 recipients, warning that dashboard filters will not appear in email. If they insist on one artifact, I drop either personalization or email and document why. I do not clone 200 dashboards.
tradeoffs: Two artifacts vs one illegal combo

interview_questions.question: Allison the sales manager needs regional copies of a master dashboard. What folder access does Help illustrate?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Editor on the folder that holds the master lets her move and adapt reports, but Editor is not Run Reports and you cannot Editor-share standard report folders.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help's Allison story is the interview answer: Editor on the master folder, then regional copies, still needing the right report permissions. I would not grant Editor on Unfiled Public or standard folders. I still choose specified versus dynamic separately. I keep Viewer for most reps. I document that saving in a folder is not the same as being able to change report metadata.
interview_questions.example: West/East clones of LAB Master Sales dashboard using Editor, not Modify All Data.
follow_ups: Why not Editor on standard folders?
Would five dashboard filters reduce clones?

interview_questions.question: Users say the emailed dashboard ignores the Product filter they use on screen.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Expected. Dashboard filters are not applied to emailed dashboards. Put the filter on the source reports or send them to the live dashboard.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I reproduce: on-screen filter Product = Hardware, email still shows all products. I explain Help's subscription limitation. I either add a Hardware filter on the source reports used by a specified-user 'Hardware' dashboard, or I tell them the live wall is the filtered experience. I also mention theme/palette and funnel totals can differ in email. I do not rebuild as dynamic to 'fix' email—that would remove subscribe entirely.
interview_questions.example: Specified dashboard with a Product filter; Monday email unfiltered.
tradeoffs: Filtered source reports vs live-only filters
Multiple subscribed dashboards vs one filtered live wall

interview_questions.question: Cannot create a sixth dynamic dashboard in Enterprise. Checklist?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Cap is 5. Check recycle bin. Confirm edition. Confirm Manage Dynamic Dashboards. Do not look at widget count first.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I count live dynamic dashboards, then recycle bin, because deleted ones still count until purged. I confirm we are not on Developer (cap 3) or Unlimited (cap 10). I check permission. If they need a sixth personalized wall, I convert some audiences to specified-user dashboards or a filtered live dashboard, or I permanently delete unused dynamics. Financial Services extra licenses exist in the limits article—Needs verification in that org before promising extras.
interview_questions.example: Four live plus two in recycle bin = cap hit at 'four visible.'

interview_questions.question: When would you avoid a dashboard entirely?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the need is a row list, a missing report type, a related-object WITH/WITHOUT, or CRM Analytics/Tableau scale—not a widget wall.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Dashboards visualize reports. If the field is missing, fix the report type. If they need WITH/WITHOUT, fix filters. If they need 50,000 rows, the 2,000-row report cap and 1,000 widget groupings will fail them—that is ANA-005/006 territory. If they need emailed detail rows, a report subscription may beat a dashboard email. I also avoid dashboards as a security bypass: specified running user is not an excuse to skip sharing design.
interview_questions.example: Request for 'dashboard of every Activity line' redirected to a filtered summary plus export policy.
follow_ups: Widget grouping cap versus report row cap?
When is CRMA the orientation answer?

interview_questions.question: Teach dashboards with the hotel video wall and break the analogy.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Screens are widgets, cameras are reports, one guard badge is specified running user, keycards are dynamic, newspapers are subscriptions that Help will not send for keycard walls. The analogy breaks on recycle-bin caps and emailed filters disappearing.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I add edition numbers 5/10/3, widget 25/20/3, recipients 500, per-user 7 or 15. I say folder Editor is a concierge key that still needs Run Reports. I refuse a library story. I finish with the interview trap: dynamic plus Monday email is two products, not one.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard the wall, then write 'NO SUBSCRIBE ON DYNAMIC' in the newspaper slot.
tradeoffs: Memorable picture vs reciting Help forbids
follow_ups: Where does the hotel analogy break?
